question: Which fictional cities saw housing costs separate most sharply from income after 2019?
audience: General readers with no prior statistical background
primary_insight: In the synthetic example, Harbor and Summit show the clearest post-2019 divergence between housing cost and income indexes.
evidence: Housing-cost index rises faster than income index in Harbor and Summit.
The gap is smaller and more stable in Cedar and Mesa.

beats.purpose: Reveal that costs and incomes do not move together.
Compare the size of the gap across four cities.
Clarify that the demo data is synthetic and not causal evidence.

visuals.purpose: Keep a common baseline while revealing divergence.
Compare the final gap across cities.

sources: Synthetic demo data included in examples/sample-data.csv
caveats: Values are illustrative only and must not be interpreted as real housing statistics.
